## Gap

batter-7r3.8 lets owned fixtures construct pools that authenticate as a separately provisioned login (PlannedPool::password_login). Session policy can only be applied through public native hooks (PgSessionProfile::reset_and_apply in after_connect/after_release). PgProfiledPool and RunledgerDatabase cannot host a fixture-managed pool, and PgProfiledPool's before_acquire verify_idle hook is crate-private, so a fixture pool cannot reproduce the application's full three-hook profiled pool or hand out a PgProfiledPool/RunledgerDatabase handle that the fixture driver closes.

## Direction

Let a planned fixture pool be declared with a PgSessionProfile so the fixture constructs it through PgProfiledPool::connect_lazy (all three hooks owned by the library, no replaceable setup callback) after login resolution, registers it before the first connectivity check, and closes it before lease cleanup. Compose with batter-nhu5's single profiled pool owner rather than adding a second one.

## Evidence

ADR-010 'Fixture login pool assessment (batter-7r3.8)'; bead comment 391 on batter-7r3.8 (consumer A's close-aware adapter).

## Outcome

An application that installs `redacting_panic_hook` can also get a structured, payload-free record of each panic in its log pipeline, without any code that can panic or block running inside the panic hook.

## Evidence

- ADR-014's survey: consumers B and C route panics into their structured logs today (by formatting `PanicHookInfo`, which discloses the payload). Moving them to `redacting_panic_hook` removes panic events from those logs. That meets the two-consumer threshold for a shared need.
- `batter-4q78` design review (2026-11-02, throwaway experiments, not repository tests): the idiomatic wrapper, a `take_hook` chain around `tracing::error!`, either discloses the payload again or, in a location-only form, turns a caught task panic into SIGABRT when the log pipe is closed. tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 reports its own write failures with `eprintln!`, which panics on a closed pipe, and std aborts on any panic raised while a hook runs (`MustAbort::PanicInHook`); `catch_unwind` inside the hook cannot contain it. No test can make subscriber code inside a hook abort-safe; only deferral avoids it.

## Candidate design (proposed, unexecuted)

- The hook keeps its stderr line and also copies the panic site into a fixed-capacity, allocation-free slot or ring (the file into a bounded byte buffer, because `Location`'s borrow ends with the hook), with a dropped-entry count.
- A registered Batter component drains the slot outside the hook and emits a `batter`-target event with file, line, column and the dropped count.
- Documented limit: an uncaught panic in `main` exits before the drain, so the stderr line remains the evidence there.

## Non-goals

Emitting `tracing` events or formatting anything inside the hook; panic classification or recovery; installing a hook from library code.

data.text: Design (2026-11-02, branch feat/redacting-panic-hook-4q78): batter_core::redacting_panic_hook() -> Box<dyn Fn(&PanicHookInfo<'_>) + Send + Sync + 'static>, #[must_use], root re-export (batter::redacting_panic_hook). Renderer takes only file/line/column; one line 'a thread panicked at <loc>; panic payload redacted' in one write through a dup of fd 2 (try_clone_to_owned). Decisions after a five-lens design critique (API invalid-state, std/Tokio source check on 1.98.1, test evidence, docs/policy, fresh-agent usability): no thread name (thread::current panics after runtime cleanup -> abort inside a hook); never take the Stderr lock, including as a fallback (lock held inside eprint! can block indefinitely; experiment reproduced a deadlock), so at the descriptor limit the hook writes nothing; contract says 'never reads, writes or forwards' because std formats panic! args before any hook; std still prints a constant nested message on PanicInHook and the full payload in a forked child before exec; closing the dup releases POSIX fcntl record locks. No witness/install() API: std cannot report the installed hook without replacing it. Hook installed first in all 9 facade examples plus reference-service main, retire_startup_controls, postgres-lifecycle main and the single-facade consumer; reference_preflight and single_facade_harness (test tooling) keep the default hook. ## Outcome

Outbound provider calls run through one library-owned, send-once HTTP exchange. The library builds the client (no redirects, no automatic replay, no ambient proxy discovery, a required connect timeout, HTTP/1.1), refuses to start once the caller's deadline is too close, derives the transport timeout from that deadline, bounds the response body under the same deadline, and returns an exhaustive outcome: not started, not dispatched (connector failure), unknown, or responded with the status retained. Its values and errors carry no URL, query, credential or body. Provider meaning, replay, idempotency, fences and reconciliation stay with applications.

## Evidence (read-only three-consumer survey, 2026-11-02; consumer identities and paths stay outside this tracker)

- All three applications hand-write the same transport rule: a connector failure proves that the attempt wrote no request bytes, any later failure leaves the outcome unknown, and a received status line is a response. The same rule appears in an owner-maintained billing library, in batter-otlp's private transport and in the reference service.
- Repairs: Consumer C needed about twelve dispatch-evidence repairs within three days, hand-copied URL stripping across 22 endpoints until a lint banned direct sends, and retrofitted start-before-deadline gates into 27 gateway methods. Consumer B lost a received status when the body stalled, and the fix was copied between provider crates. Consumer A needed four configurations to nest its transport timer inside the retry attempt cap. The billing library repaired its status-to-certainty mapping repeatedly.
- Client settings have drifted. One of C's clients disables redirects but leaves reqwest's HTTP/2 protocol-NACK replay live through feature unification, honours proxy environment variables, sets no connect timeout and leaves a credential header unmarked. A reads response bodies without a bound.
- Upstream (reqwest 0.13.x, hyper-util 0.1.20, read from source): hyper-util assigns its Connect kind only to connector or checkout failures, before the request is handed to a connection. reqwest's Display includes the full URL with its query, it has no response size limit, and its default redirect policy replays bodies and custom credential headers cross-host on 307/308.
- B's provider crates forbid any dependency named batter*, so B is evidence of need, not an adopter.

## Scope

- A new standalone package `batter-outbound`: no batter-core dependency by default, and an opt-in `operation` feature that bridges `OperationContext` deadlines and cancellation. The facade re-exports it as `batter::outbound` behind an opt-in `outbound` feature.
- This is a focused experimental extraction (ADR-014 track 1). A new ADR records why transport evidence differs from the generic provider interface ADR-014 rejected.
- A validated origin (HTTPS, or HTTP to a literal loopback address), segment-confined paths, request headers marked sensitive by construction, request preparation that surfaces every builder failure before an exchange exists, one consuming send, a bounded body and a closed outcome.

## Non-goals

Provider adapters or traits, status-to-meaning helpers, retry or replay, idempotency keys, Retry-After, dispatch fences, reconciliation, token caches, request signing, webhook ingress, HTTP/2, and operator-supplied destinations.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- Loopback fault tests pin every outcome: a refused connection is not dispatched; an expired deadline or cancellation before start is not started and the peer sees no connection; a lost response, a stalled head and cancellation in flight are unknown; a stalled, truncated or oversized body is a response with its status retained; a redirect is returned, not followed; no case sends more than one request.
- No URL, query, header value or body appears in any Debug or Display output, checked with marker values.
- Rustdoc and a runnable facade example. The new ADR, the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment, guarantees, status, references and CHANGELOG are updated, and `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes.

## Outcome

Native Runledger never persists or logs a caught handler panic payload. A handler panic records the static `job.handler_panic` code with a fixed message.

## Evidence

`runledger/runledger-runtime/src/worker/execution.rs:586-593` formats the caught payload into the `JobFailure` message (`"Job handler panicked: {payload}"`). That message is persisted in `job_queue.last_error_message`, `job_attempts.error_message`, `job_dead_letters.error_message` and the `job_events` payload. It is logged at warn on dead-letter (`runledger-runtime/src/worker/completion.rs:187-205`) and shown in the TUI. Payloads from `unwrap` and `expect` carry the Debug of the error; a reqwest error's Debug includes the full URL. This bypasses the redaction that `redacting_panic_hook` gives the hook's own output, and docs/operations.md does not list the exception. Existing tests assert only the failure code. Found during the 2026-11-02 consumer survey; no surveyed consumer depends on the text.

## Scope

- A fixed message for handler panics. The code and the PANICKED kind stay unchanged.
- Optionally, a static message for the serde arm of `From<JobExecutionError>`.
- Rustdoc on `JobFailure` constructors stating that messages are persisted verbatim and must not carry error Display or Debug text.

## Non-goals

Changing `JobFailure` constructor or field types (a native hard cut; it stays on the watch list).

- A PostgreSQL-backed runtime test panics with a secret-bearing formatted payload, then asserts that the marker is absent from job_queue, job_attempts, job_dead_letters, the job_events payload and the dead-letter log, while the code and kind are unchanged.
- A Runledger CHANGELOG "Changed" entry and docs/operations.md updated; `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes.

## Outcome

`OperationContext` gains two additive APIs:
- `run_tracked`, whose exhaustive result separates an opaque, library-constructed `NotStarted` (the factory was never invoked) from an interruption after start;
- `child_until(Instant)`, a child bounded by the earlier of its parent's deadline and the instant, inheriting cancellation.

`run` and its precedence (cancellation, then deadline, then completion) stay unchanged.

## Evidence (read-only three-consumer survey, 2026-11-02; consumer identities and paths stay outside this tracker)

- Consumer C hand-writes a pre-poll gate that reports NotStarted versus Elapsed in six helpers and about 25 sites, because `run` reports both as `Interrupted(DeadlineExceeded)`.
- Consumer A records an attempt refused before start as a definite failure, and converts externally observed absolute deadlines into contexts by hand; `child(Duration)` reports an expired budget as a configuration error.
- Consumer B deliberately treats every interruption as unknown and does not need this.
- Precedents: `BlockingError::NotAdmitted` versus `Abandoned`; batter-runlimit hand-writes `InterruptedCheck::{NotStarted, InFlight}` on top of `run`.
- The two survey reviewers split (watch versus promote-narrowed). Deliver alongside or after the outbound exchange, and adopt `run_tracked` in the reference service dispatch as the consumer contract.

## Non-goals

- Changing `run`'s precedence, or a completion-first option for arbitrary futures: polling after the deadline can start new effects.
- A minimum-remaining start floor, and retry-level in-flight evidence (watch list).
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- Paused-time tests: pre-cancelled and pre-expired contexts return NotStarted without invoking the factory; an interruption after start returns Interrupted; `child_until` never extends its parent and an elapsed instant yields an expired child.
- compile_fail doctests pin the private NotStarted constructor and the absence of From conversions.
- Rustdoc, the ADR-010 assessment, guarantees and CHANGELOG are updated, and `bash scripts/verify.sh` passes.

data.text: Decision 2026-11-02: placement is a standalone leaf package crates/batter-outbound (batter-at-rest precedent): no batter-core dependency by default; the opt-in 'operation' feature adds PreparedRequest::send_in(&OperationContext, ResponseLimit); the facade will re-export it as batter::outbound behind an opt-in 'outbound' feature. reqwest 0.13.5 (rustls), HTTP/1.1 only. Core source implemented on branch feat/outbound-exchange-3s1a (uncommitted): Origin, ConnectTimeout, ResponseLimit, Client (fixed profile: no redirects, referer off, retry::never, no_proxy, http1_only, no decompression, no hickory, 4 s pool idle, TLS>=1.2), RequestDraft/prepare (sensitive headers, reserved framing headers, dot/empty segments refused), PreparedRequest::send, exhaustive Exchange {NotStarted, NotDispatched, Unknown, Responded}. Deadline: RESERVE 50 ms + MINIMUM_ATTEMPT 50 ms; one package-owned timer bounds head and body; reqwest's per-request timeout is not used, so deadline reasons come from the package clock. Ready results win over a simultaneous timer/cancellation inside the exchange only. Local checks so far: cargo build, clippy (-D warnings -D clippy::mod_module_files) with and without 'operation', 2 sanity tests and 7 doctests pass. Tests, ADR-015, ADR-010 assessment, contracts and facade wiring in progress.

Progress 2026-11-02: build-out done by four parallel agents (tests, ADR-015 + ADR-010 assessment, contracts/package docs, facade + scripts wiring). Two implementation defects found in review and fixed: (1) url parsing deletes tab/LF/CR inside path segments before applying dot-segment rules, so a segment like '.<TAB>.' became '..' and removed a path level; prepare now refuses such segments (PrepareError::ControlCharacter) and checks that every segment survives normalization; (2) a URL that http::Uri rejects (e.g. over the http crate's length limit) passed prepare and was refused by reqwest at execution, reported as Unknown for a never-sent request; prepare now refuses it (PrepareError::InvalidUri) and Origin refuses hosts http::Uri rejects. Evidence additions: dev-dependency compiles reqwest gzip+http2 into test builds; tls_hello test (ALPN offers only http/1.1, TLS 1.2/1.3), gzip, idle-pool (4 s) and the new refusals are mutation-verified (each fails when its setting is removed). 60+ integration tests, unit test for sensitive outgoing headers, compile_fail doctests for send-once. Full scripts/verify.sh run 1 started; adversarial six-dimension review running.

## Outcome

An owner decision records whether the experimental `batter-outbound` package ships in the first crates.io release train, and if so where it sits in the publish order.

## Evidence

- The facade declares `batter-outbound` as an optional dependency behind its `outbound` feature. Cargo requires optional dependencies to be published, so publishing `batter` with that dependency makes `batter-outbound` a mandatory upload before `batter`. Its own optional `operation` feature depends on `batter-core`, so it publishes after `batter-core`.
- The publication dossier (docs/evidence/publication-dossier-2026-10-17.md, `batter-ddc`) predates the package: its tier list, name-availability check, package count and dry runs do not include it.
- ADR-014 track 2 applies two-consumer evidence to the APIs proposed for release. ADR-015 records the package as a focused experimental extraction with no adopting application root yet.

## Scope

- Name-availability check for `batter-outbound` on crates.io.
- Tier placement (after `batter-core`, before `batter`) and a packaging dry run.
- The owner's decision: ship it experimental in the first train, as `batter-otlp` is, or hold the facade's `outbound` feature until promotion.

## Non-goals

Publishing anything. This records evidence and a decision only.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The dossier or its successor lists batter-outbound with its name check, tier placement and dry-run result, and the owner's ship-or-hold decision is recorded; nothing is published.

fields.title: test_jig_integration fails intermittently: Jig 0.7.1 cannot confirm git child process-group cleanup under host process churn
fields.description: scripts/test_jig_integration.py fails intermittently because the pinned Jig 0.7.1 file-budget binary (scripts/jig -> .git/jig-tools/release-0.7.1-contract-8-runtime) reports 'Failed to run git <rev-parse|diff|status|ls-files> ... in <repository>: the process tree could not be cleaned up safely' instead of the file-budget result the test asserts. Jig spawns each git child in its own process group and confirms cleanup by scanning /proc for live group members; the failure appears when host-wide process churn is high. Evidence from 2026-11-03 (PR #77 review-fix run ed8cbdc0): two full 'python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_*.py' runs in the loop's validation worker failed with 1 and 4 such errors, all in this module, while the other 179-182 tests passed; locally the module failed 1 of 6 plain runs and 1 of 3 runs in a worker-like setsid topology and passed in isolation. No repository change in that range touched Jig paths.

## Outcome and rationale

Committed work outlives its request and may run after deployment; correlation must cross that boundary without becoming authorization or execution lifetime.

## Scope and ownership

Add the missing persisted request correlation and links to real worker attempts
through the existing reference submission and worker paths. DeliveryJobPayload
already has a version, owner, delivery identity and generation; the worker already
decodes it, checks authority/generation against current state and starts a fresh
OperationContext from its native execution budget. Reuse those mechanisms and the
completed provider reconciliation protocol, preserving their failure regressions.

Define a small validated versioned correlation representation with explicit bounds
and compatibility behavior for existing queued payloads without correlation.
Source it from server-generated request metadata, persist it with the original
submission, and link it to distinct native attempt identities after restart.
Correlation remains diagnostic: it grants no authority, replay permission,
deadline extension or ownership. Do not persist cancellation tokens, Tokio Instants,
credentials or arbitrary inbound trace/header values.

Preserve original command/effect identity and canonical provider payload matching.
Same-key replay with a new HTTP request ID must still reconcile the original command;
document which submission correlation is retained and how the replaying request is
observed without rewriting durable identity. Extend the current versioned format
compatibly; no second envelope/worker runtime or destructive migration is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Real database execution through the existing producer and worker preserves bounded submission correlation across enqueue, restart and attempts. ## Outcome and rationale

A local retry-token budget can bound amplification but cannot decide external outcome certainty, user quota consumption or durable ownership.

## Scope and ownership

Add an optional caller-owned, finite process-local retry-token budget shared by clones; no automatic replenishment, wait queue, global budget, or durable scheduler. One token authorizes one extra factory invocation after the initial call. The initial factory remains governed by the existing total context and max_attempts and consumes no retry token. Select these consumption semantics: after ReplaySafety, expected-error classification, max_attempts, provider-floor/backoff, and cancellation/deadline preflight have permitted a replay, atomically consume one token immediately before invoking that replay's factory, with no await between successful debit and invocation. Do not reserve tokens during backoff. Cancellation or deadline expiry observed by the final preflight prevents debit and factory invocation. If that preflight permits the attempt, cancellation or expiry racing afterward may still allow atomic debit and immediate counted factory invocation; no await or second cancellation gate separates successful debit from invocation. Dropping execution before this boundary consumes no token. Once invoked, the token is permanently spent, including success, returned error, timeout, cancellation, or panic. Thus there is no speculative refund and no external-effect certainty claim. Exhaustion is a distinct typed terminal outcome retaining the last concrete error and started-attempt count. Extend the opt-in execution/result boundary delivered by batter-4c4, preserving legacy signatures/error meanings and sharing its single private execution loop rather than implementing a second scheduler. Show an interactive replay-authorized profile and a durable-attempt profile with local replay disabled and the upstream runtime retaining retry ownership; do not make this optional policy a reference-protocol dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With initial capacity N shared across concurrent executions, total extra factories invoked is at most N; initial factories are uncharged, so the budget does not claim to bound new user operations. Clones share one balance, zero capacity still permits an otherwise eligible initial call, and token exhaustion never invokes the next factory or increments its attempt count.
- Barrier-driven concurrency tests contend for the final token and prove exactly one extra factory can debit it. Count actual factory invocations and retained remaining capacity; do not test only an internal counter helper.
- Cancellation, deadline expiry, or dropping the execution while waiting in backoff consumes no token. Once an extra factory is invoked, cancellation, timeout, returned error, success, or unwinding panic does not refund it. Tests observe the actual before/after boundary; no delay-based guess stands in for it.
- ReplaySafety::Never, classifier Stop, max_attempts exhaustion, and a provider floor leaving insufficient total time consume no retry token. Cancellation or total expiry observed by final preflight is interruption without debit. A race after that preflight may consume a token only together with its counted invocation; no-await does not make clock/cancellation/decrement one atomic operation. Token exhaustion is distinguishable from AttemptsExhausted/InsufficientBudget and retains the last E and actual count; it is not fabricated as cancellation or a returned application error.

The durable profile permits one local factory per upstream attempt; the interactive profile requires caller replay authorization. Provider/effect/durable lifetime counts remain owned by the reference protocol tasks.
- A single opt-in execution combines per-attempt caps, shared tokens, jitter and provider floors. A started extra attempt that times out spends its token; interruption/backoff before invocation spends none. Distinct typed attempt/total/token outcomes retain prior E and actual counts, and all existing entrypoints keep their meaning.

## Outcome

An owner decision records whether the experimental `batter-outbound-http` package ships in the first crates.io release train, and if so where it sits in the publish order.

## Evidence

- The facade declares `batter-outbound-http` as an optional dependency behind its `outbound-http` feature. Cargo requires optional dependencies to be published, so publishing `batter` with that dependency makes `batter-outbound-http` a mandatory upload before `batter`. Its own optional `operation` feature depends on `batter-core`, so it publishes after `batter-core`.
- The publication dossier (docs/evidence/publication-dossier-2026-10-17.md, `batter-ddc`) predates the package: its tier list, name-availability check, package count and dry runs do not include it.
- ADR-014 track 2 applies two-consumer evidence to the APIs proposed for release. ADR-015 records the package as a focused experimental extraction with no adopting application root yet.

## Scope

- Name-availability check for `batter-outbound-http` on crates.io.
- Tier placement (after `batter-core`, before `batter`) and a packaging dry run.
- The owner's decision: ship it experimental in the first train, as `batter-otlp` is, or hold the facade's `outbound-http` feature until promotion.

## Non-goals

Publishing anything. This records evidence and a decision only.
